items.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
items.abstract: CliffCompaction is an autocompaction technique for long-horizon coding agents that significantly reduces costs (up to 50%) by only truncating or dropping information, never rephrasing it. This method maintains or improves performance on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench, enabling more efficient test-time scaling and achieving state-of-the-art results. Its core contribution lies in cost-effective context management without sacrificing fidelity.

items.title: PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment
items.abstract: This paper addresses the lack of a clear mathematical definition for token-level credit in reinforcement learning for LLMs. It proposes three regularity conditions (Completeness, Prefix Consistency, and Neutrality) that uniquely define token-level credit, providing a unified framework for existing algorithms. This characterization leads to an improved actor-critic training procedure and explains why certain existing methods, like RLOO, align with token-level credit signals.

items.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces recursive self-improvement for AI research agents, where an agent iteratively modifies and improves its own code. The core method, AIDE^2, proposes, benchmarks, and retains code changes that enhance performance on AI R&D tasks. Its main contribution is demonstrating a path to overcome diminishing returns in AI R&D by enabling sustained, autonomous self-improvement.

items.title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces REFLEX, an LLM agent architecture that uses a fast, typed decision layer (Jev) for efficient, selective control. REFLEX calls a powerful LLM only when confidence is low or generation is necessary, significantly reducing computation while maintaining high task success. The core contribution is demonstrating when and where this selective control mechanism offers computational benefits, identifying limitations related to action-set size and accuracy of the routing mechanism.

items.title: Flash-dLLM: IO-Aware KV Caching and Parallel Decoding for Fast, Memory-Efficient Diffusion LLMs
items.abstract: Flash-dLLM tackles the inference inefficiency of Diffusion LLMs by addressing I/O bottlenecks in KV caching and parallel decoding. Its core method is an I/O-aware fused KV-cache kernel that minimizes redundant memory transfers. This optimization enables efficient KV-cache-driven draft-and-verify decoding, leading to faster and more memory-efficient dLLM inference without retraining.

items.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
items.abstract: This paper introduces A2M, a two-stage framework for hijacking agents that use the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A2M first optimizes tool metadata to attract agent invocation and then uses execution traces to manipulate tool outputs, steering agents towards malicious outcomes. The contribution lies in demonstrating a practical and effective method for exploiting semantic supply-chain risks in MCP ecosystems, achieving high malicious invocation rates and successful attacks across various scenarios.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of benign versus adversarial MCP interactions. The upper panel depicts a standard execution trace using legitimate tools. The lower panel illustrates the A2M attack, where an adversary exploits semantic matching to attract the agent to a malicious tool and utilizes crafted return payloads to manipulate the agent’s reasoning trajectory.

items.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper proposes a new method for LLM reasoning that moves beyond simple repeated sampling. Instead of generating many similar answers, it learns to generate diverse "concepts" (like hints or strategies) that guide the LLM towards more varied and potentially correct solutions. The core contribution is a trainable "concept generator" that is optimized to improve the success rate of a fixed answer generator on complex reasoning tasks.

items.title: From Alignment to Access Control: A Framework for GenAI Policy Enforcement
items.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for systematically analyzing and dissecting existing approaches to policy enforcement in Generative AI (GenAI) applications. Its core contribution is to move beyond the current fragmented landscape by offering a principled methodology and recommendations for better policy definition and enforcement, aiming to improve GenAI security and compliance.
items.figure_caption: Screenshot depicting vibe coding incident that resulted in a production database deletion [ 64 ] .

items.title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that greedy decoding in LLMs is not precision-invariant, meaning the same model and prompt can produce different outputs when using BF16 versus FP16 precision. The core contribution is an empirical analysis showing that small precision differences cascade into significant output divergence, primarily determined by the margin between the top two predicted tokens at the model's head. This analysis also leads to testable predictions about how to improve output consistency, which are experimentally validated.

items.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes "Growing Harness," a method to train LLM agents by learning reusable code for recurring control decisions, rather than repeatedly asking the LLM to make them. By analyzing task failures and using an optimizer, the system iteratively builds a shared harness of executable code. This allows LLM calls to be reserved for task-specific reasoning, leading to more efficient and capable agents.

items.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
items.abstract: This paper identifies the "Proximity Trap," where irrelevant nearby information hinders LLMs from attending to crucial distant evidence. To combat this, they introduce LYRA, a novel mechanism that reshapes context retrieval to prioritize relevant distant information while maintaining positional awareness. This approach significantly improves LLM performance on long-context tasks by better utilizing distant evidence.

items.title: Double Descent and Malign Overfitting in Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates overfitting in diffusion models, challenging the conventional "benign overfitting" observed in standard deep learning. The authors demonstrate that diffusion models exhibit "malign overfitting," where excessive parameters lead to catastrophic memorization rather than improved generalization. They resolve this paradox by showing that while an interpolation peak exists, it occurs at a higher parameter count ($p \sim nm$) than expected, and a significant rise in test loss begins much earlier ($p \sim n$).

items.title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper proposes MAGIC, a reinforcement learning framework for generating mixed-granularity agent graphs for LLM-based multi-agent systems. MAGIC's core method involves incrementally constructing these graphs by selecting functional roles and their collaboration granularity locally, allowing for fine-grained control and reusable patterns. The key contribution is enabling efficient exploration of the complex graph construction space with dense rewards, overcoming limitations of previous approaches that used uniform granularity.
items.figure_caption: Fixed-granularity organizations versus MAGIC ’s mixed-granularity construction for an API-update task.

items.title: On the Lexical Superstition of Large Language Models for Code Comprehension: Re-evaluation on Code of Low Lexical Quality
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) overemphasize lexical cues in code comprehension. They introduce a framework called Face/Off to rename identifiers while preserving program structure, then evaluate LLMs under various renaming conditions. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLMs exhibit a pervasive "lexical superstition," meaning they are heavily influenced by identifier names, even when those names are misleading, and struggle to rely on underlying code semantics.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold text marks output phrases associated with identifiers in the code, and italic text marks phrases associated with method names. In the lower example, the summary follows the misleading identifiers even though they conflict with the implementation. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold and italic text mark phrases associated with identifiers in the code; in one example, the generated summary follows misleading names rather than the implementation.

items.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
items.abstract: Agensh is a novel multi-agent system that overcomes scalability limitations of traditional orchestrator-based frameworks. Its core method is a self-organized cooperation loop where agents asynchronously gather context, assign tasks, act, and share findings without a central coordinator. This decentralized approach allows for significantly improved scaling of organizational intelligence.

items.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies
items.abstract: This paper argues that observing only behavior is insufficient to identify social norms in LLM societies, as it can stem from various underlying mechanisms. The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that measures agents' reported expectations alongside behavior. Their contribution lies in demonstrating that eliciting these expectations and incorporating social learning and selection mechanisms leads to more robust and interpretable norm emergence, distinct from mere behavioral convergence.
items.figure_caption: Our framework for mechanism ablation of social norm emergence in generative agent societies. The agents play a public good games in groups where they can discuss and create expectations about appropriate behavior.

items.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper argues that **calibration**, the alignment of a language model's confidence with its accuracy, is a crucial but overlooked aspect of LLM evaluation. The core method proposed is to **integrate standard calibration metrics into existing benchmarks**, which already provide the necessary confidence and correctness data. The main contribution is highlighting how widespread miscalibration hinders trustworthy LLM development and deployment, impacting areas like LLM-as-a-judge and active learning.

items.title: HySparse2: Hybrid Sparse Attention with Two-Level KV Sharing
items.abstract: HySparse2 proposes a hybrid sparse attention architecture to efficiently handle long contexts in agents. It employs a two-level KV sharing strategy: outer-level KV Bridging uses a YOCO-style structure with hybrid attention for full-attention layers, and inner-level KV Reuse refines long-context retrieval with token-level sparsity. This approach improves prefill efficiency, reduces KV-cache storage, and enhances retrieval accuracy for long contexts.

items.title: Semantic Abstraction for Natural Language Inference: a Methodological Framework for Discovering and Compensating Semantic Knowledge and Reasoning Gaps in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes a methodological framework to address semantic abstraction challenges in Large Language Models (LLMs) for Natural Language Inference (NLI). It constructs higher-level semantic knowledge by reconfiguring lexical-semantic relations into a flexible network, enabling LLMs to discover and compensate for reasoning gaps. This approach leads to more consistent and agreeable responses in NLI tasks.

items.title: A Semiotics-Aware Framework for Evaluating Fidelity and Coverage in Natural Language Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating Natural Language Generation (NLG) by assessing "semiotic alignment" between texts. It proposes two metrics, Semiotic Fidelity and Semiotic Coverage, which go beyond simple lexical overlap to capture differences in contextual meaning and discourse references. The framework's contribution lies in providing a more nuanced evaluation of NLG output, revealing that LLM alignment with human data is sensitive to generation parameters like sampling temperature.
items.figure_caption: Semiotic profiles of “Venus” : human vs. LLM (top left); semiotic triads for astronomer (top right), classicist (bottom left), astrologer (bottom right).

papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) overemphasize lexical cues in code comprehension. They introduce a framework called Face/Off to rename identifiers while preserving program structure, then evaluate LLMs under various renaming conditions. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLMs exhibit a pervasive "lexical superstition," meaning they are heavily influenced by identifier names, even when those names are misleading, and struggle to rely on underlying code semantics.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold text marks output phrases associated with identifiers in the code, and italic text marks phrases associated with method names. In the lower example, the summary follows the misleading identifiers even though they conflict with the implementation. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold and italic text mark phrases associated with identifiers in the code; in one example, the generated summary follows misleading names rather than the implementation.

papers.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
papers.abstract: Agensh is a novel multi-agent system that overcomes scalability limitations of traditional orchestrator-based frameworks. Its core method is a self-organized cooperation loop where agents asynchronously gather context, assign tasks, act, and share findings without a central coordinator. This decentralized approach allows for significantly improved scaling of organizational intelligence.

papers.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies
papers.abstract: This paper argues that observing only behavior is insufficient to identify social norms in LLM societies, as it can stem from various underlying mechanisms. The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that measures agents' reported expectations alongside behavior. Their contribution lies in demonstrating that eliciting these expectations and incorporating social learning and selection mechanisms leads to more robust and interpretable norm emergence, distinct from mere behavioral convergence.
papers.figure_caption: Our framework for mechanism ablation of social norm emergence in generative agent societies. The agents play a public good games in groups where they can discuss and create expectations about appropriate behavior.

papers.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper argues that **calibration**, the alignment of a language model's confidence with its accuracy, is a crucial but overlooked aspect of LLM evaluation. The core method proposed is to **integrate standard calibration metrics into existing benchmarks**, which already provide the necessary confidence and correctness data. The main contribution is highlighting how widespread miscalibration hinders trustworthy LLM development and deployment, impacting areas like LLM-as-a-judge and active learning.

papers.title: HySparse2: Hybrid Sparse Attention with Two-Level KV Sharing
papers.abstract: HySparse2 proposes a hybrid sparse attention architecture to efficiently handle long contexts in agents. It employs a two-level KV sharing strategy: outer-level KV Bridging uses a YOCO-style structure with hybrid attention for full-attention layers, and inner-level KV Reuse refines long-context retrieval with token-level sparsity. This approach improves prefill efficiency, reduces KV-cache storage, and enhances retrieval accuracy for long contexts.

papers.title: Semantic Abstraction for Natural Language Inference: a Methodological Framework for Discovering and Compensating Semantic Knowledge and Reasoning Gaps in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a methodological framework to address semantic abstraction challenges in Large Language Models (LLMs) for Natural Language Inference (NLI). It constructs higher-level semantic knowledge by reconfiguring lexical-semantic relations into a flexible network, enabling LLMs to discover and compensate for reasoning gaps. This approach leads to more consistent and agreeable responses in NLI tasks.

papers.title: A Semiotics-Aware Framework for Evaluating Fidelity and Coverage in Natural Language Generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating Natural Language Generation (NLG) by assessing "semiotic alignment" between texts. It proposes two metrics, Semiotic Fidelity and Semiotic Coverage, which go beyond simple lexical overlap to capture differences in contextual meaning and discourse references. The framework's contribution lies in providing a more nuanced evaluation of NLG output, revealing that LLM alignment with human data is sensitive to generation parameters like sampling temperature.
